overrides: month winner and runner_up: the Nov 4 and Nov 9 Polish wins are used so the Nov 10 Game of the Week (also the top November score, 67.2) is not shown twice on the page
year runner_up: the Sep 23 rook-endgame mate returns (it was only set aside while it was also the Game of the Month)
week runner_up: the Nov 10 queen-sacrifice mate (59.9) was picked over two higher-scoring wins decided by opponent errors by move 3 and a 61.7 win against a lower-rated opponent
eligibility: rated standard-chess win in 2026 (both sites, no Chess.com coach/bot games, no variants)
excluded: opponent berserked (Lichess WhiteBerserk/BlackBerserk header, or opponent started with under 60% of the base clock); this removes the +560 win (the opponent berserked)
excluded: abandonments; wins on time before move 20; any game under 20 moves; Lichess opponents on the provisional 1500 default

excluded: any game where he made a blunder: an engine "Blunder" judgment, or any of his moves where the eval swung 2.00+ pawns against him (mate capped at ±10). Comeback-from-a-blunder wins therefore do not qualify

requires per-move engine data, so blunder-free play can be verified (Chess.com Aug 2–Oct 1 and Oct 26–Nov 11 2026 via local Stockfish, plus Chess.com Game Review where it exists; Lichess server-analysed games)
data_note: Chess.com data through Nov 11, 2026 (578 new games since the Nov 2 refresh: Nov 3–11). No Lichess games since Sep 23.

week.label: Game of the Week
week.window: 2026-11-10 → 2026-11-13 ET (week in progress; no games after Nov 11)
week.window_note: Chess.com only (no Lichess games since Sep 23). 21 of the 97 wins of 20+ moves were blunder-free on our Stockfish pass and Chess.com Game Review.

winner.caption: 1-minute bullet as Black against a 1405, out of 1.d4 c5. 12...Bxa1 won the exchange, the queens came off, and his rooks took over the second rank: 26...Rxf2+ started a chase that drove the king to d1, 33...Rgxc2 collected the knight and 36...Ra1# finished it. 93.3 accuracy on Chess.com Game Review, no blunders and 24.3s left on his clock.
winner.reason: Beat a 1405 (he was 1418) by mate (36...Ra1#) with 93.3 accuracy / 22.6 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
winner.why: Highest score (67.2) of the 21 blunder-free wins from Nov 10 to Nov 13, and a real game: his eval only stayed above +3.00 for good from move 21. The next two by score (64.0 and 62.5) were decided by opponent errors by move 3.

runner_up.caption: 1-minute bullet as Black against a 1542 in a Sicilian. 19...Rxc2+ won White's queen, and he signed off with a Chess.com Brilliant: 28...Qc1+ gives the queen back on c1, 29.Rxc1 is White's only legal move, and 29...Rxc1# is mate on the same square. No blunders on Chess.com Game Review (80.7 accuracy) and 16.4s left on his clock.
runner_up.reason: Beat a 1542 (he was 1537) by mate (29...Rxc1#) with 80.7 accuracy / 48.1 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
runner_up.why: Scored 59.9. Picked over the 64.0 and 62.5 wins, which were decided by opponent errors by move 3, and over a 61.7 win against a 1372: this one beat a stronger opponent (1542), has a Chess.com Brilliant and ends in a queen-sacrifice mate.

month.label: Game of the Month
month.window_note: 41 blunder-free wins: 40 from Nov 3 to Nov 11 and the Nov 2 Benoni. The top-scoring November game (Nov 10, 67.2) is the Game of the Week, so it is not repeated here.

winner.caption: 1-minute bullet as White against a 1616, out of the Polish (1.b4). 12.Nxd6+ forked the king and the b7 bishop, 13.Nxb7 cashed in, and after the queens came off he hunted the king to h5 with his pawns: 39.g5+ Kh5 40.Ng7# is mate. No blunders on our Stockfish pass, 94.0 accuracy and 9.4s left on his clock.
winner.reason: Beat a 1616 (he was 1619) by mate (40.Ng7#) with 94.0 accuracy / 27.6 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
winner.why: Best November fair fight (63.6) once the Nov 10 Game of the Week is set aside so one game isn't shown twice. The 64.0 Nov 10 win ranks above it on score but was decided by an opponent error on move 3, so it was passed over. There is no Chess.com Game Review for Nov 4, so the accuracy is our local Stockfish figure.

runner_up.caption: 1-minute bullet as White against a 1479, another Polish (1.b4). 14.Bxg7 picked up a bishop, the d-pawn marched all the way to 33.d8=Q, the c-pawn followed with 41.c8=Q, and two queens finished it with 43.Qh5#. No blunders on our Stockfish pass, 94.0 accuracy and 12.2s left on his clock.
runner_up.reason: Beat a 1479 (he was 1491) by mate (43.Qh5#) with 94.0 accuracy / 36.3 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
runner_up.why: Scored 63.1, half a point behind the Nov 4 Polish: the same mate finish and full length, but against a lower-rated opponent (1479 vs 1616). Shown here so the Nov 10 Game of the Week isn't repeated on the page. There is no Chess.com Game Review for Nov 9, so the accuracy is our local Stockfish figure.

year.label: Game of the Year
year.window_note: Winner unchanged. No November win beats its 68.8.

winner.caption: His best-played game of 2026: as Black in 10-minute rapid against a 2131, 98.5 accuracy, ACPL 10.3 and not even an inaccuracy. He took over after 12...Nd5, won the d-file and queened a pawn before his opponent resigned on move 49.
winner.reason: Beat a 2131 (he was 2068) by resignation after 49...Qxh4 with 98.5 accuracy / 10.3 ACPL and no blunders (Lichess 600+0)
winner.why: It is the only eligible 2026 win over a 2100+ opponent (the next highest is 1990). It has the year's highest accuracy (98.5), full ACPL points (10.3) and a perfect 8/8 clean score, and its opponent-strength score of 12.2 is second only to 12.7. The runner-up (67.2) has the edge on contest and mate, but it beat a 1665 and scored only 1 clean point. The next candidates, #3 (66.1) and #4 (65.9), are bullet wins over opponents rated 1469 and 1574.
winner.key_move_note: from here his eval stayed at +3.00 or better to the end
winner.standout_why: punished the opponent's previous move, eval +0.47→+2.78

runner_up.caption: Seventy-one moves of 1-minute bullet as Black against a 1665, with no blunders and only one mistake: level until move 37, then he out-ground the rook endgame, promoted on h1 and mated with 71...Ra5# with about 3 seconds left.
runner_up.reason: Beat a 1665 (he was 1653) by mate (71...Ra5#) with 94.3 accuracy / 16.9 ACPL and no blunders (Chess.com 60)
runner_up.why: Back as Year runner-up (67.2) now that it is no longer the Game of the Month on the page. It was the original #2 of the year and was only set aside because it repeated the September Month winner. The Nov 10 Game of the Week scores the same 67.2 but already fills the Week slot.
runner_up.key_move_note: from here his eval stayed at +3.00 or better to the end
runner_up.standout_why: engine's top move; punished the opponent's previous move, eval +6.77→+10.00
